recipes.description: Red curry paste (Prik Gaeng Phed) is a bold, aromatic blend of spices and herbs, essential for making Thai red curries. Its rich flavors bring a perfect balance of heat, depth, and complexity to dishes.

steps.detail: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the dried red chilies, shallots, garlic, coriander roots, lemongrass, and kaffir lime zest until fragrant and slightly charred. Stir frequently to prevent burning.
Allow the toasted ingredients to cool slightly before transferring them to a mortar and pestle or food processor. Grind or pound until a smooth paste forms.
Mix in the cumin, turmeric, peppercorns, and salt, then grind or process until fully blended.
If the paste is too thick, add a splash of water to loosen it.
Keep the red curry paste in an airtight container in the fridge, where it will stay fresh for up to a month.

tips: For a milder curry paste, remove the seeds from the dried red chilies before roasting.
You can adjust the amount of spices to your preferred heat level.

recipes.description: Green curry paste is a bold, aromatic blend that serves as the heart of many Thai dishes, especially green curries. Its signature bright green color comes with a balanced mix of spicy, sweet, and slightly bitter flavors.

steps.detail: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the green chilies, shallots, garlic, coriander roots, lemongrass, and kaffir lime zest until fragrant and lightly charred. Stir occasionally to prevent burning.
Allow the toasted ingredients to cool slightly before transferring them to a mortar and pestle or food processor. Grind or pound until a smooth paste forms.
Mix in the cumin, turmeric, salt, and cilantro (if using), then grind or blend until fully incorporated.
If the paste is too thick, add a splash of water to loosen it.
Keep the green curry paste in an airtight container in the fridge, where it will stay fresh for up to a month.

tips: If you prefer a milder curry paste, simply remove the seeds from the green chilies before roasting them.

recipes.description: Massaman curry paste stands out from other Thai curries with its unique blend of warm, aromatic spices. Its rich, complex flavors come from ingredients like cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.

steps.detail: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the dried red chilies, shallots, garlic, coriander roots, lemongrass, kaffir lime zest, cumin, turmeric, cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, nutmeg, and black peppercorns until fragrant and lightly charred. Stir occasionally to prevent burning.
Allow the toasted spices to cool slightly before transferring them to a mortar and pestle or food processor. Grind or pound until a smooth paste forms.
Mix in the shrimp paste, then grind or blend until fully combined.
If the paste is too thick, add a splash of water until it reaches your desired texture.
Keep the massaman curry paste in an airtight container in the fridge, where it will stay fresh for up to a month.

tips: For the most authentic texture and flavor, consider using a mortar and pestle instead of a food processor. It helps release the essential oils from the ingredients.

recipes.description: Yellow curry paste (Prik Gaeng Karee) is a bold and aromatic condiment widely used in Thai cuisine, especially in yellow curries. Its vibrant yellow color comes with a perfect balance of sweet, savory, and mildly spicy flavors.

steps.detail: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the dried red chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric, cumin, black peppercorns, and salt until fragrant and lightly charred. Stir occasionally to avoid burning.
Allow the roasted ingredients to cool slightly before transferring them to a mortar and pestle or food processor. Grind or pound until a smooth paste forms.
If the paste is too thick, add a splash of water to reach your desired texture.
Keep the yellow curry paste in an airtight container in the fridge, where it will stay fresh for up to a month.

tips: Adjust the levels of salt, sugar, and acidity to taste. A little tamarind paste or lime juice can brighten the overall flavor.

recipes.description: Panang curry paste has a rich, creamy, and subtly sweet flavor. It's an essential ingredient in Thai Panang curry and brings a deep, flavorful kick to many dishes.

steps.detail: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the dried red chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and peppercorns until fragrant. Stir occasionally to avoid burning.
Allow the toasted ingredients to cool slightly, then grind them into a coarse paste with a mortar and pestle or food processor.
Mix in the shrimp paste and salt to the coarsely ground mixture. Continue grinding until it becomes a smooth paste.

tips: Shrimp paste gives Panang curry paste its unique flavor. If you find it too strong, start with a smaller amount and adjust to taste.

recipes.description: Som Tam is a famous Thai salad loved for its spicy, sour, and sweet flavors. It's made with shredded green papaya, chili peppers, lime juice, fish sauce, and a few other key ingredients.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons long beans, cut into small pieces

steps.detail: Slice the green papaya into thin strips.
Put the garlic and chilies into a mortar and lightly pound them.
Add palm sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice. Mix well.
Add tomatoes and long beans. Lightly pound and mix.
Add the shredded green papaya and dried shrimp. Gently pound and mix everything together.
Add more lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, or chili depending on your taste.
Transfer the Som Tum to a plate and top with roasted peanuts.

tips: Serve with vegetables (e.g. cabbage, string beans, etc.).
Thai people love to eat sticky rice with Papaya Salad.

recipes.name_thai: ส้มตำอีสาน
recipes.description: Som Tum Isan (ส้มตำอีสาน) is a traditional northeastern Thai papaya salad. It has a strong spicy, sour, salty, and savory flavor. Unlike Som Tum Thai, Isan-style Som Tum often uses fermented fish (pla ra) and usually does not focus on sweetness.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons long beans, cut into pieces

steps.detail: Wash and cut the vegetables. Shred the green papaya. Slice the green papaya into thin strips.
Put the garlic and chilies into a mortar and lightly pound them.
Add pla ra, fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Mix well.
Add tomatoes and long beans. Lightly pound and mix.
Add the shredded green papaya and gently pound and mix everything together.
Add more lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, or chili depending on your taste.
Transfer the Som Tum to a plate and serve it with fresh vegetables.

tips: Serve with vegetables (e.g. cabbage, string beans, etc.).
Thai people love to eat sticky rice with Papaya Salad.

recipes.description: Larb is a traditional dish from northeastern Thailand and Laos. It is especially popular in the Isan region of Thailand. Larb Neua is spicy, sour, salty, and fresh. It has a delicious herbal and nutty flavor from fresh herbs and toasted rice powder. Larb Neua is often served with sticky rice and fresh vegetables such as cabbage, cucumber, and herbs.

steps.detail: Slice the shallots and chop the spring onions, mint, and coriander.
Heat a pan over medium heat. Add the minced beef and cook until it is fully cooked. Stir occasionally.
Turn off the heat. Add fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes, sugar, and toasted rice powder. Mix well.
Add the shallots, spring onions, mint, and coriander. Mix gently until everything is well combined.
Transfer the beef salad to a serving plate. Serve with fresh vegetables and sticky rice.

tips: If you like to add spiciness to the dish, you can add green chilies.
It is recommended that you eat it with cucumbers, eggplants and vegetables.

recipes.name_en: Thai Crying Tiger Steak (Suea Rong Hai)
recipes.description: Suea Rong Hai is a popular Thai-Isan grilled beef dish, especially in northeastern Thailand. It is juicy, smoky, spicy, sour, and salty. The beef is grilled and served with a spicy and sour dipping sauce called Nam Jim Jaew. It is often served with sticky rice and Nam Jim Jaew.
ingredients: Nam Jim Jaew: 2 tbsp fish sauce
Nam Jim Jaew: 1 tbsp lime juice
Nam Jim Jaew: 1 tbsp toasted rice powder
Nam Jim Jaew: 1–2 tbsp chili flakes
Nam Jim Jaew: 1 tbsp finely chopped shallot
Nam Jim Jaew: 1 tbsp chopped coriander
Nam Jim Jaew: 1 tbsp chopped spring onion

steps.detail: First, mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, fish sauce, black pepper, and vegetable oil in a bowl. Add the beef and mix well. Let it marinate for 15–30 minutes.
Heat a grill or pan over medium-high heat. Grill the beef for about 4–5 minutes on each side, depending on how well-done you like it.
Remove the beef from the grill and let it rest for about 5 minutes. This helps keep the meat juicy and tender.
In a small bowl, mix fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, toasted rice powder, chili flakes, shallot, coriander, and spring onion. Stir well.
Cut the beef into thin slices. Serve the grilled beef with Nam Jim Jaew, a spicy and sour Thai dipping sauce.

tips: Slice the steak against the grain to make it easier to chew.
Opt for marbled cuts of beef like sirloin or rib-eye, these are great for grilling due to their distributed fat content.

recipes.description: This traditional Thai cooking method involves steaming food in banana leaf parcels. Begin by preparing the bamboo shoots and making a flavorful spice paste. Mix the bamboo shoots and pork with the paste, then wrap the mixture tightly in banana leaves and steam until fully cooked.
ingredients: 15 g fermented fish sauce (pla ra), optional

steps.detail: Peel and slice the bamboo shoots into thin pieces. Boil the bamboo shoots in water for about 15 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Wash the yanang leaves. Rub or squeeze the leaves with water to extract the green juice. Strain the juice and set it aside.
Slice the pork into thin pieces. Finely chop the garlic, shallots, lemongrass, and chilies. Chop the spring onions, dill, and Thai basil.
Put the bamboo shoots and pork into a large bowl. Add the chopped herbs and chilies. Add fish sauce, salt, rice flour, and fermented fish sauce (pla ra), if using. Mix everything well.
Put the mixture into a pot. Pour in the yanang broth. Bring it to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the pork is fully cooked. Stir occasionally.
Add Thai basil, dill, and spring onions. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Turn off the heat.
Serve hot with steamed sticky rice.

recipes.description: Nam Phrik Ong is a traditional food from Northern Thailand. It is a popular dish from Lanna cuisine. Nam Phrik Ong is a thick chili dip made with minced pork, tomatoes, chilies, garlic, and shallots. It has a rich, slightly spicy, and slightly sour taste. Usually eat Nam Phrik Ong with sticky rice, fresh vegetables, steamed vegetables, and crispy pork rinds.

steps.detail: Chop the tomatoes and shallots. Mince the garlic. Cut the dried chilies into small pieces.
Put the dried chilies, garlic, and shallots in a mortar. Pound them until they become a smooth paste. Add the shrimp paste and mix well.

Add the minced pork. Stir well and cook until the pork is no longer pink. Add the chopped tomatoes and water, stir well. Cook over medium heat until the tomatoes are soft. Simmer until the mixture becomes thick.
Add fish sauce and sugar. Add fermented soybean paste if desired. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Turn off the heat. Sprinkle with spring onions and coriander. Serve warm with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.

tips: Origin: Northern Thailand (Lanna / Northern Thai).
Main ingredients: pork and tomatoes. Taste: savory, slightly spicy, and slightly sour.
Usually served with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.

recipes.description: Khao Soi is a famous noodle dish from Northern Thailand, especially Chiang Mai. Its history was influenced by cultural and trade connections with Myanmar, Laos, and southern China. The dish was also influenced by Yunnanese Muslim traders, who brought noodle and curry cooking traditions to the region. Local people later adapted the dish using local ingredients and flavors.
ingredients: 400 g chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps.detail: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Chop the shallots and garlic. Slice the ginger and red onion.
Heat the oil in a pot. Add the curry paste, shallots, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir well. Cook until the outside of the chicken is no longer pink.
Add the coconut milk and water or chicken stock. Add curry powder, fish sauce, and sugar. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until the chicken is fully cooked.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package instructions. Drain well.
Put the noodles in a bowl. Pour the curry soup and chicken over the noodles. Top with crispy fried noodles. Serve with pickled mustard greens, red onion, chilies, and lime.

tips: Cuisine: Lanna / Northern Thai. Main ingredients: egg noodles, chicken, coconut milk, and curry paste.
Taste: creamy, savory, mildly spicy, and aromatic.
Usually served with: crispy noodles, pickled mustard greens, onion, and lime.

recipes.description: Gaeng Hung Lay Chicken is a Northern Thai curry influenced by Burmese and Shan cuisine. The traditional dish is made with pork, but chicken can also be used. It is known for its rich, aromatic flavor from ginger, garlic, tamarind, and dried spices. Unlike many Thai curries, it usually contains no coconut milk.
ingredients: 500 g chicken thighs, cut into pieces
50 g Gaeng Hung Lay curry paste

steps.detail: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Slice the ginger and shallots, and chop the garlic.
Heat the oil in a pot. Add the curry paste and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir well. Cook until the outside of the chicken is no longer pink.
Add the shrimp paste, curry powder, fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar. Stir well.
Add the water or chicken stock. Add the ginger, garlic, shallots, and dried chilies. Cover and simmer on low heat until the chicken is tender and the sauce becomes thick.
Add the roasted peanuts and stir gently. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve hot with steamed rice.

tips: Cooking style: slow-cooked until the chicken is tender.
Cultural influence: Burmese and Shan cuisine.
Usually served with steamed rice.

recipes.name_en: Hot and Sour Prawn Soup (Tom Yum Goong)
recipes.description: Tom Yum Goong is a popular Thai soup known for its spicy, sour, and tangy flavors. The combination of lemongrass, galangal, lime juice, and chili peppers creates a unique and flavorful broth.

steps.detail: Clean the shrimp and slice the lemongrass, mushrooms, tomato, and galangal. Tear the kaffir lime leaves.
Bring the water or stock to a boil. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and chilies.
Add the mushrooms and tomato.
Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink and are fully cooked.
Add fish sauce and sugar. Turn off the heat, then add lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Garnish with chopped coriander and serve hot.

tips: Serve the soup while still hot and garnish on the top with pieces of spring onion and coriander.

recipes.name_en: Red Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Phed Gai)
recipes.description: Thai Red Curry is a spicy and aromatic blend of red curry paste, coconut milk, a protein like chicken or pork, and vegetables. It's a blend of sweet, salty, spicy, and umami, combined into one.
ingredients: 300 g chicken breast or thigh, sliced

steps.detail: Slice the chicken, bamboo shoots, and red bell pepper. Prepare the curry paste and other ingredients.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the red curry paste and stir for about 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add half of the coconut milk. Stir well and cook until the curry becomes fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir until it is almost cooked.
Add the remaining coconut milk, water, bamboo shoots, and bell pepper. Add fish sauce and sugar. Simmer until the chicken is fully cooked.
Turn off the heat and add Thai basil. Stir gently.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with Thai basil and sliced red chili.

tips: While you can use a different kind of squash or whatever vegetables are available to you, such as Thai eggplant, pineapple, winter melon, and bamboo shoots.

recipes.name_en: Green Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Keow Wan Gai)
recipes.description: Thai Green Curry made by freshening up store bought curry paste or with a homemade green curry paste! Whichever way you go, the one essential step to make a really great green curry is to fry off the curry paste. Cook with chicken or even entirely meat-free. With a sauce this good, you can put anything in it – and it will taste amazing!
ingredients: 100 g Thai eggplant, cut into pieces

steps.detail: Slice the chicken, Thai eggplant, bamboo shoots, and red chili.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the green curry paste and stir until fragrant.
Add half of the coconut milk. Stir well and cook for about 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir until it is almost cooked.
Add the remaining coconut milk, water, Thai eggplant, and bamboo shoots. Add fish sauce and sugar. Simmer until the chicken and vegetables are cooked.
Turn off the heat. Add Thai basil and sliced red chili. Stir gently.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

tips: Feel free to add other vegetables like bamboo shoots, zucchini, or mushrooms.
Serve with jasmine rice and Thai rice noodles.

recipes.description: Gaeng panang moo, or Thai panang pork curry, is an irresistibly creamy dish that's perfect for your busy weeknights. It's a total crowd favorite, with its gently spiced, mild flavors that you can easily tweak to taste. Serve this saucy dream with fragrant jasmine rice, it's perfect for planning ahead or whipping up on the fly.

steps.detail: Slice the pork and red chili. Thinly slice the kaffir lime leaves.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the Panang curry paste and stir until fragrant.
Add half of the coconut milk. Stir well and cook until the curry paste is fragrant and well mixed.
Add the sliced pork and stir until the pork is almost cooked.
Add the remaining coconut milk, water, fish sauce, and sugar. Stir well and simmer until the pork is fully cooked.
Add the sliced kaffir lime leaves and Thai basil. Stir gently and turn off the heat.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced red chili and kaffir lime leaves.

tips: Opt for pork neck or loin for their tender and juicy qualities.
Reducing the coconut milk allows it to release its natural oils, intensifying the flavor and aroma of the curry.
Serve immediately with jasmine rice.

recipes.name_en: The "Original" Thai Basil Stir Fry (Pad Kra Pao Moo)
recipes.description: Pad Ka-Prao is a popular Thai dish known for its spicy, savory, and fragrant flavors. It typically consists of stir-fried minced meat (often pork, beef, or chicken) with basil leaves, chili peppers, and other ingredients.
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, for frying eggs

steps.detail: Chop the garlic and Thai chilies. Pick the basil leaves and prepare the minced pork.
Heat the oil in a wok or pan. Add the garlic and chilies. Stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the minced pork. Stir-fry until the pork is fully cooked.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and water. Stir well.
Add the holy basil leaves. Stir quickly until the leaves become soft and fragrant. Turn off the heat.
Heat oil in a pan. Fry the eggs until the edges are crispy and the whites are cooked.
Serve the Pad Kra Pao Moo with steamed jasmine rice and a crispy fried egg.

tips: Serve immediately with jasmine rice and egg.
Pad Kra Pao is a versatile dish that can be customized to your preferences. Enjoy!

recipes.name_en: Thai Sweet and Sour Chicken (Pad Priew Wan Gai)
recipes.description: "Pad Priew Wan," or Thai sweet and sour stir-fry chicken, is a popular takeout option that can now be enjoyed at home. This flavorful Thai dish features a variety of healthy vegetables and your choice of protein, all coated in a delightful sweet and sour sauce.

steps.detail: Slice the chicken and vegetables. Cut the pineapple and tomato into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the oil in a wok or pan. Add the garlic and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it is almost cooked.
Add the onion, cucumber, bell pepper, tomato, and pineapple. Stir-fry well.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, ketchup, sugar, vinegar, and water. Stir well and cook until the sauce is slightly thick.
Add spring onion and stir briefly. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

tips: Serve with jasmine rice.
Feel free to add your favorite vegetables, protein, or garnish.

recipes.name_en: Stir-fried Vegetables with Shrimp (Pad Pak Goong)
recipes.description: Pad Pak Goong is a simple Thai stir-fried dish made with shrimp and fresh vegetables. Stir-frying is a common cooking method in Thai cuisine because it is quick, easy, and keeps vegetables fresh and slightly crunchy. Thai-style stir-fried vegetables are usually seasoned with ingredients such as oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and garlic. Different vegetables and proteins can be used depending on what is available.
ingredients: 50 g broccoli, cut into small pieces

steps.detail: Peel and clean the shrimp. Wash and cut all the vegetables into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a wok or pan. Add the garlic and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry until they turn pink and are almost cooked.
Add the carrot, broccoli, baby corn, and cabbage. Stir-fry well.
Add oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water. Stir well and cook until the vegetables are tender but still slightly crunchy.
Add spring onion and stir briefly. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

tips: What does "Pad Pak Goong" mean? Pad (ผัด) = stir-fry, Pak (ผัก) = vegetables, Goong (กุ้ง) = shrimp. So, Pad Pak Goong = Stir-fried Vegetables with Shrimp.

recipes.description: Pad See Ew is a popular Thai stir-fried noodle dish. The name "Pad See Ew" means "stir-fried with soy sauce." The dish uses wide rice noodles cooked with soy sauce, eggs, vegetables, and meat. Pad See Ew is part of Thailand's tradition of stir-fried noodle dishes and is influenced by Chinese cooking techniques and ingredients. It became a popular everyday meal in Thailand and is now well known in Thai restaurants around the world.
ingredients: 250 g fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai)

steps.detail: Slice the chicken into thin strips. Wash and slice the Kale. Mince the garlic. Gently separate the noodles and mix them with dark soy sauce until evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan. Add the garlic and chicken. Stir-fry until the chicken is cooked.
Move the chicken to one side of the pan. Crack in the eggs and stir until they are almost cooked.
Add the fresh rice noodles. Gently stir-fry with the chicken and eggs.
Add light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and water. Add the Kale and stir-fry until the vegetables are cooked.
Serve hot and enjoy immediately.

tips: What does "Pad See Ew" mean? Pad (ผัด) = stir-fry, See Ew (ซีอิว) = soy sauce. So, Pad See Ew = Stir-fried Noodles with Soy Sauce.

recipes.description: Pad Thai is one of Thailand's most famous noodle dishes. It became especially popular in Thailand during the 1930s–1940s, when rice noodles were promoted as an economical and convenient food. The dish combines rice noodles with ingredients such as tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, eggs, bean sprouts, and peanuts. Shrimp is one of the popular choices of protein. Pad Thai later became famous internationally and is now commonly served in Thai restaurants around the world.
ingredients: Pad Thai sauce: 2 tbsp fish sauce
Pad Thai sauce: 2 tbsp tamarind paste

steps.detail: Soak the dried rice noodles in warm water until they become soft but still slightly firm. Drain well.
Peel and clean the shrimp. Chop the garlic chives and garlic. Prepare the eggs, bean sprouts, and peanuts.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a large pan. Add the shrimp and stir-fry until they turn pink and are almost cooked. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, fry the garlic until fragrant. Add the eggs and scramble gently.
Add the drained noodles. Add fish sauce, tamarind paste, sugar, and water. Stir-fry until the noodles are soft and well coated with the sauce.
Return the shrimp to the pan, add bean sprouts and garlic. Stir-fry briefly so the vegetables stay fresh.
Serve hot with crushed peanuts, lime wedges, and chili flakes.

tips: What does "Pad Thai Goong" mean? Pad (ผัด) = stir-fry, Thai (ไทย) = Thai, Goong (กุ้ง) = shrimp. So, Pad Thai Goong = Thai Stir-fried Noodles with Shrimp.

recipes.description: Massaman Curry is a Thai curry with strong historical connections to Muslim and Persian-influenced cooking traditions. It developed in Thailand and became part of Thai cuisine through cultural exchange. Unlike many spicy Thai curries, Massaman Curry uses warm spices such as cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. It also commonly contains potatoes, onions, peanuts, and coconut milk. Chicken Massaman Curry is now a popular Thai dish and is well known internationally.
ingredients: 400 g chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps.detail: Cut the chicken and potatoes into pieces. Slice the onion and prepare the peanuts and spices.
Heat the oil in a pot. Add the Massaman curry paste and stir until fragrant.
Add half of the coconut milk. Stir well and cook until the curry paste is well mixed and fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir until the outside of the chicken is cooked.
Add the remaining coconut milk, water, cinnamon, cardamom, and bay leaf. Stir well.
Add the potatoes and onion. Simmer over low heat until the chicken and potatoes are tender.
Add fish sauce, tamarind paste, and sugar. Stir well. Add the roasted peanuts.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

tips: You can switch up the protein with other meats, seafood, or tofu. Don't forget to adjust the cooking time accordingly.
If you're watching your fat intake, chicken breast is a better choice than thighs.

recipes.description: Moo Hong is a traditional dish from Southern Thailand, especially popular in Phuket and nearby areas. It is made by slowly cooking pork belly with garlic, black pepper, spices, and soy sauce. The dish has influences from Chinese cooking traditions, reflecting the historical Chinese communities in Southern Thailand.
ingredients: 500 g pork belly, cut into large pieces

steps.detail: Crush the garlic, shallots, black peppercorns, and coriander roots together. Cut the pork belly into large pieces.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic, shallots, black pepper, and coriander roots. Stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and stir-fry until the outside of the pork is lightly browned.
Add soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and palm sugar. Mix well so the pork is covered with the sauce.
Add water, cinnamon, and star anise. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer until the pork is tender and the sauce becomes rich and slightly thick. Stir occasionally.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

tips: Cooking method: slow braising.
Taste: savory, slightly sweet, rich, and aromatic.

recipes.description: Hat Yai fried chicken is a popular Southern Thai dish beloved for its crispy outer layer with tender marinated meat, often paired with sticky rice and a dipping sauce. With a fragrant blend of herbs and spices, it's a popular street food favorite in Hat Yai. While the recipe varies from chef to chef, the one thing that is always included are the crispy fried shallots. We marinate ours in a dark and rich seasoning made with lots of garlic, coriander root, peppercorns, soy sauce, dark sweet soy sauce, sugar, and salt, then we use the marinade to make a thick batter for the chicken.
ingredients: For the Chicken: 800 g chicken pieces
For the Chicken: 2 tbsp coriander roots, chopped
For the Chicken: 1 tbsp black peppercorns
For the Chicken: 1½ tbsp fish sauce
For the Chicken: 1 tbsp soy sauce
For the Chicken: 1 tbsp oyster sauce
For the Chicken: 100 g rice flour
For the Chicken: 50 g all-purpose flour
For the Chicken: 500 ml vegetable oil, for frying
For the Fried Shallots: 100 g shallots, thinly sliced
For the Fried Shallots: 2 tbsp crispy fried shallots, for serving

steps.detail: Crush the garlic, coriander roots, and black peppercorns together. Mix with fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar.
Put the chicken into a large bowl. Add the marinade and mix well. Cover and marinate for at least 30 minutes. For better flavor, marinate in the refrigerator for several hours.
Mix rice flour, all-purpose flour, and water in a bowl. The mixture should be thick enough to lightly coat the chicken.
Dip each piece of chicken into the flour mixture. Make sure the chicken is evenly coated.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Carefully add the chicken and fry until golden brown and fully cooked. Turn the chicken occasionally so it cooks evenly.
Fry the sliced shallots until golden and crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Drain the fried chicken well. Top with crispy fried shallots. Serve hot with sticky rice and sweet chili sauce.

tips: For the most practical recipe, count the 30-minute marinating period separately from active preparation/cooking time.
